details: U.S. President Trump formally notified Congress that military hostilities with Iran concluded on April 7th, with his 60-day war authority expiring on May 1st. This declaration, coupled with a new ceasefire proposal from Iran, led to a drop in WTI crude oil prices below $102 per barrel. This reduction in energy market risk premium provided a macro tailwind for Bitcoin, which climbed back above $78,000.
title: US Declares End to Iran Hostilities, Oil Falls, Bitcoin Reclaims $78K

details: White House top crypto adviser Patrick Witt indicated that lawmakers have reached a compromise on the "Clarity Act," a significant Bitcoin and crypto market structure bill. The bill, which could be advanced in May, aims to establish a clear regulatory framework for the digital asset space, including stablecoins. This legislative clarity is anticipated to unlock billions in institutional capital.
title: US Lawmakers Near Deal on Landmark Crypto Market Structure Bill

details: Amid ongoing U.S. sanctions and recent military conflicts, Iran is increasingly leveraging cryptocurrencies for financial transactions. Reports indicate that Iran is converting its cryptocurrency holdings into renminbi to facilitate trade and bypass the dominance of the U.S. dollar, thereby accelerating de-dollarization efforts.
title: Iran Intensifies Crypto Use to Bypass US Sanctions

details: Israel's Capital Market Authority approved the issuance and distribution of BILS, a shekel-pegged stablecoin, following a two-year pilot program. Simultaneously, Pakistan's State Bank issued new regulations allowing its regulated entities to open bank accounts for licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) and their customers. These developments indicate a growing trend in various nations to integrate local currencies with blockchain technology and provide clearer banking access for crypto businesses.
title: Israel Approves Shekel-Pegged Stablecoin, Pakistan Eases Crypto Banking
